7.0.s.en: (1) The sealing of the children of God

7.0.0.en: God allowed St. John to see another vision before the opening of the seventh seal. He looked and saw four angels at the four corners of the earth, as though the earth had become a square flat surface before him, holding the four winds of the earth. We do not know how an angel holds winds ... but John saw and knew by the Spirit and wrote what he saw. The meaning here is that everything is subject to the authority and command of God, who has entrusted His angels with carrying out His will in protecting the earth from the violent winds that may come from any direction. If these winds were released, they would uproot all the trees, the seas would overflow because of them, and fierce storms that end life on earth would grow violent.

7.0.1.en: Wind: it signifies the justice of God in punishing the wicked.

7.1.0.en: Another angel ascending from the east: most of the Fathers affirmed that this angel is a new appearance of Christ in the Revelation of John, for the following reasons:

7.1.1.en: (1) He comes forth from the rising of the sun, for He is "Light of Light" and He is "the light of the world."

7.1.2.en: (2) He has the seal of God with Him, for the presence of the king's seal in his hand means that he has the same authority as the king.

7.1.3.en: (3) It is He who called out and commanded the angels not to harm the earth, and this is from His authority and by His will.

7.1.4.en: There is another opinion which says that he is one of the angels, but from among the principal and highest orders of them.

7.1.5.en: Christ came forth in a radiant appearance from the rising of the sun, carrying the authority of God His Father and the seal of the Living One (the Holy Spirit), and He gave a command to the four angels who hold the four winds of the earth to remain as they were, holding the winds, so that no harm would come upon the earth or injury to anyone until all the servants of God have been sealed with the living seal, which is the anointing of the Holy Spirit granted to us in the oil of the Holy Myron, by the signing on our foreheads and our bodies.

7.1.6.en: To whom it was given to hurt: this does not mean that they have authority to do this by their own will, for the will here is God's alone and His absolute command. As for the word "given," it means that God created them with a special power to carry this out when He commands them.

7.1.7.en: From these two verses we conclude that the final plagues will not come before God distinguishes His children from the wicked, so that nothing may harm them (see the parable of the tares and the wheat in Mt 13:30).

7.1.8.en: My beloved brother ... how great is the anointing with which we were anointed in the sacrament of the Holy Myron, and by which the Holy Spirit dwelt within us, so that we became sealed for God, bearing His name as His children and moving about as living, holy temples. Yet some of us do not realize the greatness of this gift and its responsibility. Would that we all hasten to listen to St. Paul when he warns us not to quench the Spirit (1 Thess 5:19) or grieve Him (Eph 4:30). So hasten always to repentance, my friend, that you may enjoy the work of the divine Spirit within you.

7.2.0.en: I heard: that is, St. John did not see the believers during their sealing, but learned by hearing from one of the angels.

7.2.1.en: A hundred and forty and four thousand: the meaning and the numbers here are spiritual and symbolic. This number is the product of the 12 tribes of the Church of the Old Testament × the 12 disciples, the fathers of the Church of the New Testament × a thousand, and the number one thousand here points to heavenly perfection ... The number as a whole means that everyone of God's people of old who waited in hope for the redemption of the Son, and everyone who accepted His redemption through the proclamation of the Gospel and of the Apostles in the Church of the New Testament, has become one of those sealed before the throne of God and enjoying Him.

7.2.2.en: Every tribe ... the children of Israel: of course the word Israel here comes in its spiritual meaning, for it is not reasonable that the Jews who rejected faith in Him and did not accept it are the "sealed," they who made the infant Church taste terrors of torment and persecution ... What confirms that the speech here is spiritual is that he mentioned the word tribes, and we know that there are at present no tribes in Israel, for they no longer keep their genealogies or their tribes.

7.3.0.en: In these four verses St. John begins to explain and detail what he summarized in the previous verse. He makes clear that the number of a hundred and forty-four thousand is twelve thousand sealed from each of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel ... Here it is important for us to point out the following ...

7.3.1.en: (1) In the order of the tribes here, the chronological order was not observed, as Jacob did when he mentioned the names of his sons in the order of their birth (Gen 49), beginning with his firstborn Reuben.

7.3.2.en: (2) The tribe of "Dan" is not mentioned because it worshipped idols in the land it possessed (Judg 18:29-31). So everyone who departs from the worship of God by worshipping a strange worship has his name blotted out of the book of life (Deut 29:18-25). Likewise, an ancient Jewish tradition says that the Antichrist will come from the tribe of Dan). Irenaeus, Against Heresies 5:30.((3) Joseph is mentioned as a tribe instead of the tribe of Ephraim his son, because the tribe of Ephraim fell into idolatry and allied with the enemies against Judah (Isa 7:17), and the Lord rejected them from before Him (Jer 7:15). (4) Joseph did not have a tribe of his own, for in return for his faithfulness of old he received double compared with his brothers, in two full portions for his children, so that his son "Manasseh" became a tribe and his son "Ephraim" a tribe ... and now he receives a full portion before God. In this there is a spiritual meaning and teaching that reminds us of what the Lord said: "Whosoever hath, to him shall be given, and he shall have more abundance" (Mt 13:12), "You were faithful in little, I will set you over much" (Lk 19:17). (5) It is also noticeable that the tribe of Levi, which after the Law was not mentioned as an independent tribe and did not inherit a portion in the land because it was the tribe of service ..., now stands before God in return for its service, which is the noble service of the priesthood before God.

7.3.3.en: Would that we therefore learn to strive as much as we are able, so that we obtain what Joseph obtained, namely a double portion, and not be negligent and become like "Dan" or "Ephraim," who lost everything.

7.4.0.en: After this: we move on to a new vision. In the first scene St. John was looking on the earth ... but here he continues his vision in heaven, although the subject is one: the first was the sealed Church, and here it is the triumphant Church.

7.4.1.en: A great multitude: this is a joyful scene that St. John saw, for the number here cannot be counted ... and it is something that pours all hope into the heart of the Church striving on earth ... For despite the many spiritual wars, the violence of Satan and the many temptations ... there is the work of the saving grace of God, and despite the enemies who persecute the Church in order to destroy her faith, we find that those who enter heaven are beyond number, for God is her keeper and the One who overshadows her.

7.4.2.en: All nations ... tongues: God's plan of salvation is not limited to one people to the exclusion of another. God came and became incarnate for the redemption of all mankind, so everyone who accepts His redemption and holds fast to the right faith will inherit and stand before Him who sits on the throne and before the slain Lamb. There is no distinction in heaven between color, race or language. Is He not the One "who will have all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth" (1 Tim 2:4)? White robes: they signify purity and holiness, for none but the pure enter heaven, while holiness is acquired by a person through his nearness to God.

7.4.3.en: Palm branches: there are no material things in heaven, and so the palm branches here are a spiritual scene that points to victory and triumph, since people used to receive the processions of victorious commanders after wars with palm branches; see also (Jn 12:13). St. John saw a great multitude that he could not count, from the different peoples of the earth, in purity, joy and victory.

7.4.4.en: Take courage, beloved ... for you have a place in heaven where there is glory, so take all care that no one steals your crown from you.

7.5.0.en: And they cried: the crying with a loud voice here is the cry of joy, jubilation and praise, for they are in a state of joy beyond imagining, and how could it not be so when they are victorious and enjoy the sight of their Redeemer and Savior!?!

7.5.1.en: Salvation to our God: this is the hymn of praise and victory, for in the rapture of their everlasting joy they proclaim the secret of this happiness ... and this hymn has two meanings:

7.5.2.en: The first: victory belongs to our God, the Almighty, the Conqueror who went forth conquering (Rev 6:2). He conquered Satan, bound him and stripped him of his authority (Lk 10:18), and conquered death and trampled it (1 Cor 15:55), and released all those who were held captive in Hades and brought them out to Paradise (Eph 4:9). The second meaning: our God is the secret of our salvation, and we would not have been saved without Him, meaning that God gave them salvation and they return the credit to its owner, thanking Him for having accomplished their victory.

7.5.3.en: Him that sitteth upon the throne, and the Lamb: that is, the hymn is offered to the Father and the Son in the same measure, and this is evidence of the equality of the two hypostases.

7.6.0.en: All the heavenly creation, with all its orders (ranks), took part in the praise and the contrite, joyful worship before God, and in their praise they offered Him the seven attributes of greatness and honor, which indicate the perfection of His attributes ... All of this was explained in detail in (ch. 4:10-11), (ch. 5:12-14).

7.7.s.en: (2) Explanation by the elder (one of the priests)

7.7.0.en: God willed for St. John, and for us also, not to be content with watching the wonderful scene but also to know some of its secrets. For this reason one of the twenty-four priests approached him with a question whose purpose was to urge St. John to knowledge. His question meant: do you know who these are who are clothed in white robes, what their secret is, and why they stand here?! And because St. John does not know all the mysteries, he answered him with courtesy and respect: "Sir, thou knowest" (v. 14). This is a humility that teaches us to turn with our questions to the priests and fathers of the Church concerning what is hard for us to understand or apply.

7.8.0.en: This heavenly priest answered St. John as follows:

7.8.1.en: These are they which came out of great tribulation: the tribulation here may be the tribulation to which every Christian is exposed in his private life, in persecution or temptation which he bears with thanksgiving, or a persecution that passes over the whole Church and reaches the point of martyrdom for the faith. The great tribulation here may also be a reference to the period of the Antichrist's presence on earth and the wars and afflictions that will accompany his presence.

7.8.2.en: The spiritual meaning is what the Lord Christ announced repeatedly, that there must be tribulation in the world (Mt 24:9), (Jn 16:3), and what St. Paul also affirmed, that suffering and tribulation are the price of the glory revealed in us before God (Rom 8:17). Have washed their robes, and made them white: "washed" and "made white" are two inseparable actions, for washing leads to whiteness. The meaning is that for these who overcame the great tribulation, the secret of their purity, holiness and victory was the blood of the Lamb. A Christian has no strength apart from the blood of Christ, for salvation, steadfastness and purity are founded on "His precious blood."

7.8.3.en: The washing and whitening remind us of two inseparable sacraments of the Church. The first is the washing from sin in the sacrament of confession, when the priest reads the absolution and casts the filth of sin off the repentant penitent, and the whitening is actually accomplished in the blood of the only-begotten Son, so that after Communion a person goes forth pure and clean, having been united with the most holy Body and Blood of Christ.

7.8.4.en: We must all not lose heart before tribulation and pain ... however much sufferings increase upon us, let us look to heaven and trust that we have a crown. For what Stephen saw of the beauty of heaven at the time of his martyrdom made him think lightly of the temporary, limited pain compared with the unlimited glory (Acts 7).

7.9.0.en: Therefore: that is, because they passed through the great tribulation and did not lose heart, and also were cleansed by the blood of the Lamb, which cleanses from all sin (1 Jn 1:7). Are they before the throne of God: this is the dearest and greatest reward, that a person should stand in the presence of God, offering praise with the heavenly beings without ceasing, for he has become part of heaven and of the heavenly creation itself. The words "in His temple" signify absolute nearness to the unlimited divine Essence, despite the multitude of numbers beyond counting (v. 9), for each one will be near to God, enjoying Him inside His temple. Note: the word temple here does not refer to a limited place, for God is not limited by place, and likewise the expression "Him that sitteth on the throne" ... the meaning here is spiritual, and the scene is presented to us as far as the human mind can grasp it.

7.9.1.en: Shall dwell among them: in the Greek language, "will overshadow them," which is a stronger expression than the meaning of constant presence before God, for it means divine embrace, encompassing and keeping of every soul that has completed its struggle and has a place before the throne and inside the temple.

7.9.2.en: My beloved brother, our standing in the Church and seeing her sanctuary and altar remind us of this wonderful heavenly scene. Indeed, the Church during the Liturgy is heaven itself, and you are called to enjoy heaven here in the Church, to stand before the divine Presence, which we shall continue, by the grace of Christ, in His eternal Kingdom. So do not let laziness or any other hindrance keep you away from what you are called to.

7.10.0.en: They shall hunger no more, neither thirst any more: St. John continues to describe the state of happiness that the victors feel. The words "they shall not hunger or thirst" first mean that they are satisfied with Christ and the divine Essence, and they are in a state of constant spiritual quenching, so the sensations of the body no longer "occupy or trouble us, and nothing diminishes the splendor of the enjoyment of God.

7.10.1.en: The word "any more" leads us to another meaning, which is that these had been subjected to torture by hunger and thirst for the sake of faith and love of God, or they were hungry and thirsty for righteousness in Christ (Mt 5:6), and now the time has come for their compensation for all their suffering. For God in His justice does not forget anyone's labor, but repays him a hundredfold, and without doubt the compensation of heaven cannot be compared with any compensation on earth.

7.10.2.en: Neither shall the sun light on them, nor any heat: that is, no new burden of trials will be upon them. Solomon describes trials as the burning sun (Song 1:6), and likewise there will be no new troubles, "heat"; and how could this be when God Himself overshadows them, shelters them and shepherds them (v. 15).

7.11.0.en: The previous chapter ended with its talk about "the day of the wrath of the Lamb" and His vengeance on the wicked (ch. 6:17), and here the picture is completely different with His holy children, for He shepherds them Himself and gives Himself to them, in a beautiful and eloquent picture and in a manner easy for human beings to imagine, and He presents to us some of these pictures. Shall lead them unto living fountains of waters: this verse is connected with what came in (v. 16" (They shall not thirst ..."), for the secret of their not thirsting is their being quenched by spiritual springs that never run dry or fail, since Christ alone has become their source, and this reveals to us a new secret of the mysteries of eternity ... there we drink and receive and grow ... for eternity is not a static scene but a constant spiritual movement that carries us from perfection to perfection.

7.11.1.en: And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes: this brings us back to the justice of God and His compensation for every labor and every pain His children endured during their life on earth, ... so take courage, beloved, and bear with thanksgiving everything you pass through. How beautiful is this wonderful spiritual picture, as Christ stretches out His tender hand to pat us and wipe the tears from our eyes ... It is of course well known that there are no real tears in eternity, for the bodies are spiritual and luminous, but the meaning is a beautiful one that expresses the tenderness of God, His compassion and His compensation of His children for all their sufferings.

7.11.3.en: "God's warnings by the first four trumpets"

7.11.4.en: Introduction to chapter eight: chapter six carried the first six seals, which foretold some of the things coming upon the earth until the end of time. After the reassuring heavenly scene that St. John saw in chapter seven, he brings us back to the seventh and last seal, which in turn carries a new group of seven, the seven trumpets, of which the first four occupy chapter eight, while the rest come in
